ap_chemistry-m01.stem: A chemist needs a buffer with a pH of $7.7$. Which conjugate acid-base pair (HCO₃⁻ / CO₃²⁻ ($\mathrm{p}K_a=10.33$); NH₄⁺ / NH₃ ($\mathrm{p}K_a=9.25$); HCOOH / HCOO⁻ ($\mathrm{p}K_a=3.75$); H₂PO₄⁻ / HPO₄²⁻ ($\mathrm{p}K_a=7.21$)) would be most effective, assuming equal total concentrations are available for each?

options.text: H₂PO₄⁻ / HPO₄²⁻
options.why: A buffer works best when the pH is within about one unit of the pKa; H₂PO₄⁻ / HPO₄²⁻ has pKa = 7.21, only 0.49 units from the target pH of 7.7.

options.text: NH₄⁺ / NH₃
options.why: Its pKa of 9.25 is 1.55 units from the target pH of 7.7, more than the one unit over which a buffer works well.

options.text: HCOOH / HCOO⁻
options.why: This pair has the strongest acid shown (pKa = 3.75), but that is 3.95 units from the target pH of 7.7, so it would resist pH changes poorly.

options.text: HCO₃⁻ / CO₃²⁻
options.why: This pair has the weakest acid shown (pKa = 10.33), but that is 2.63 units from the target pH of 7.7, so it would resist pH changes poorly.

ap_chemistry-m02.stem: A student dissolves a solid in water in a calorimeter in three trials and records the temperatures (table). Which claim about the dissolving process is best supported by the data?

stimulus.description: Temperature of water before and after a solid is dissolved

options.text: The process is neither exothermic nor endothermic, because each mixture reached a steady final temperature.
options.why: Confuses reaching a steady temperature with no energy transfer between the process and the solution.

options.text: The process is endothermic, but the data cannot support that claim because the final temperatures differ from trial to trial.
options.why: Treats ordinary trial-to-trial scatter as a reason to ignore three trials that all show the same direction of change.

options.text: The process is endothermic: the temperature of the solution changed by an average of $-2.5\,^{\circ}\text{C}$, so the dissolving process absorbed energy from the solution.
options.why: The temperature changes in the three trials are -2.5, -2.3, -2.6 °C (mean -2.5 °C); a temperature decrease of the solution means energy was absorbed from the solution by the process, so the process is endothermic.

options.text: The process is exothermic: the temperature of the solution changed by an average of $-2.5\,^{\circ}\text{C}$, so the dissolving process released energy to the solution.
options.why: Reverses the link between the direction of the temperature change and the direction of energy flow.

ap_chemistry-m03.stem: The reaction $2\mathrm{A}(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B}(g)$ is at equilibrium. The volume of the container is halved at constant temperature. Which statement correctly describes the response of the system?

options.text: The system shifts toward the products, because the reaction quotient Q becomes smaller than K, so more products must form until Q equals K again.
options.why: For this disturbance halving the volume doubles both concentrations, so Q = [B]^1/[A]^2 is multiplied by 2^(1 − 2) = 0.5; Q is therefore smaller than K, so the system shifts toward the products until Q equals K again.

options.text: The system shifts in neither direction, because the concentrations of A and B do not change, so Q still equals K.
options.why: After this disturbance Q is smaller than K, not equal to K, so the system does not stay at equilibrium.

options.text: The system shifts toward the reactant, because the reaction quotient Q becomes larger than K, so more reactant must form until Q equals K again.
options.why: After this disturbance Q is smaller than K, not larger than K, so the system does not shift toward the reactant.

options.text: The system shifts toward the reactant, because the equilibrium constant changes.
options.why: Believes that a change in concentration or volume changes the value of K, which depends only on temperature.

ap_chemistry-m04.stem: The gaseous reaction $\mathrm{A(g) \rightleftharpoons B(g)}$ is at equilibrium in a rigid, closed container at constant temperature with $[\mathrm{A}]=0.5\text{ M}$ and $[\mathrm{B}]=0.2\text{ M}$, so $K_c=0.4$. A student predicts what happens when the concentration of A is suddenly increased by adding more A at constant volume and temperature. Which prediction is correct?

options.text: The net reaction proceeds toward the products, because immediately after the change $Q_c$ is less than $K_c$.
options.why: After the change Q = 0.222, compared with the unchanged K = 0.4: Q is less than K, so the net reaction proceeds toward the products until Q equals K again.

options.text: The net reaction proceeds in neither direction (no net change), because immediately after the change $Q_c$ is equal to $K_c$.
options.why: This answer takes Q to be equal to K and the net reaction to go in neither direction (no net change), but after the change Q = 0.222 and K = 0.4, so Q is less than K.

options.text: The net reaction proceeds toward the reactants, because immediately after the change $Q_c$ is greater than $K_c$.
options.why: This answer takes Q to be greater than K and the net reaction to go toward the reactants, but after the change Q = 0.222 and K = 0.4, so Q is less than K.

options.text: The net reaction proceeds toward the products, because immediately after the change $Q_c$ is greater than $K_c$.
options.why: The direction is right, but Q is not greater than K here: Q = 0.222 and K = 0.4.

ap_chemistry-m07.stem: In the unit cell of an ionic solid, the X ions are located as follows: 1 at the center of the cell. The Y ions are located as follows: 12 at the edge centers. (An ion at a corner is shared by 8 cells, at a face center by 2 cells, and at an edge center by 4 cells.) What is the empirical formula of the compound?

options.text: $\mathrm{XY_{6}}$
options.why: Doubles the number of anions counted in the cell.

options.text: $\mathrm{X_{3}Y}$
options.why: Inverts the ratio of cations to anions.

options.text: $\mathrm{XY_{3}}$
options.why: Ions on corners, faces, and edges are shared by neighboring cells, so each counts as a fraction: X contributes 1 ion(s) and Y contributes 3 ion(s) per cell, a ratio of 1:3.

options.text: $\mathrm{XY_{12}}$
options.why: Counts every ion position as a whole ion, ignoring that corner, face, and edge ions are shared.
